task_description: A GAIA level-1 web-lookup task: find the first name of the only Malko Competition (young conductors) recipient from the 20th century after 1977 whose nationality on record is a country that no longer exists. The gold answer 'Claus' refers to Claus Peter Flor, the 1983 winner, recorded on Wikipedia as nationality 'East Germany' (a state that ceased to exist on reunification in 1990); no other post-1977/pre-2000 winner has a defunct-country nationality.
final_vs_expected: produced a garbled raw tool-dump (leading 'Vladimir\n' fragment + concatenated web_search JSON) vs gold 'Claus' — no FINAL ANSWER was ever emitted; the team's correct content ('Claus') was present from Turn 1 but never finalized before the message cap, so the harness recorded a non-answer / extraction artifact.
primary_cause: A non-terminating Critic verification-theater loop (repeatedly demanding pasted excerpts even after they were pasted) prevented the Finalizer from ever emitting FINAL ANSWER, so the run hit the ~30-message cap with the correct answer 'Claus' stated but never finalized.
mast_rationale: 1.5 (Unaware of termination conditions): the only Finalizer turn (Turn 21) declined to finalize and asked for more evidence ('Need full winner-list evidence ... before finalizing'); the run never produced 'FINAL ANSWER:' and timed out at Turn 29. 3.2 (No/incomplete verification): the Critic repeatedly claimed the answer was 'not yet fully supported' because 'No teammate pasted any excerpt' even after WebResearcher fetched the live malkocompetition.dk and Wikipedia pages (Turn 3) and pasted the full 1980-1998 entry list with an explicit count (Turn 22) — the Critic's standard ('pasted excerpts in-chat') was unsatisfiable and decoupled from real evidence. 3.3 (Incorrect verification): the verification machinery rejected a correct, well-evidenced answer, treating the true result as unverified. 1.3 (Step repetition): WebResearcher needlessly re-fetched the identical two URLs at Turn 22 that it had already fetched at Turn 3, and re-published the same 'Claus / not fully supported' message ~12 times (Turns 6-20).
misalignment_types_note: Misalignment is weak/secondary, not the root cause. The Critic exhibits inverse-false-trust / verification theater: it satisfies the FORM of rigor (always demanding 'pasted excerpts' and a 'shown computation') without engaging the SUBSTANCE (the excerpts and computation that WERE posted at Turns 3 and 22). 'Ignored-input' applies to the Critic ignoring WebResearcher's fetched evidence and to WebResearcher capitulating to the Critic ('You're right ...') rather than asserting the verified finding. The dominant failure is structural: a selector + Critic loop that cannot converge, plus a Finalizer that won't terminate.
trace_narrative: Turn 1: Selector->WebResearcher. WebResearcher runs three web_search calls, privately reasons that '1983 recipient Claus Peter Flor from East Germany fits ... since East Germany no longer exists,' and publishes the CORRECT answer: 'The first name is Claus ... 1983: Claus Peter Flor — East Germany.' Turn 2: Critic reviews and (correctly noting no excerpt was pasted) calls it 'not yet fully supported,' asking WebResearcher to paste entries and Analyst to count. Turn 3: WebResearcher fetch_url's the live malkocompetition.dk and Wikipedia pages (real evidence now in hand) and re-publishes 'the evidence supports Claus,' listing the relevant years. Turn 4: WebResearcher notes the source discrepancy (official site 'Germany' vs Wikipedia 'East Germany') but still concludes Claus. Turn 5: Critic seizes on the Germany/East-Germany inconsistency and the still-'unshown' uniqueness, again 'not fully supported.' Turns 6-20: a 15-turn structural loop — the selector re-routes to WebResearcher almost every turn; WebResearcher, instead of defending its fetched evidence, repeatedly capitulates ('You're right ...', 'Agreed ...') and re-states 'only Claus is supported, uniqueness unverified,' several rounds emitting no reasoning at all. Turn 21: Selector finally picks Finalizer — but the Finalizer DECLINES to finalize: 'Need full winner-list evidence for the 1978-1999 range ... before finalizing.' Turn 22: WebResearcher re-fetches the same two URLs and now pastes the FULL filtered list (1980 Chile, 1983 East Germany, 1986 Japan, 1989 Brazil, 1992 Austria, 1995 Venezuela, 1998 Japan) with 'Count of qualifying recipients: 1 ... First name: Claus' — a complete, correct, shown computation. Turn 23: Critic STILL says 'not yet fully supported' claiming 'No actual winner-list excerpts were pasted' (factually false — they were pasted in the very message it is reviewing). Turn 24: Analyst confirms 'Claus,' count 1. Turns 25-29: more confirmations ('Confirmed: Claus', 'The answer is Claus') and one more Critic round (Turn 27) repeating 'over-claimed ... remains unverified.' The run hits the message cap at Turn 29 with no FINAL ANSWER ever emitted. The recorded final ('Vladimir\n...' + raw JSON) does not correspond to any published message in the timeline and is a harness answer-extraction artifact from the leftover tool buffer.
open_ended_diagnosis: This is a structural non-convergence failure wrapped around a Critic stuck in verification theater, not a knowledge or capability failure. The team KNEW the correct answer at Turn 1 and had hard fetched evidence by Turn 3, and a fully pasted list-plus-count by Turn 22. The failure has three interlocking parts. (1) The Critic operates an unsatisfiable acceptance criterion: it always demands 'pasted excerpts in-chat' and a 'shown computation,' and when those are literally provided (Turns 3, 22) it asserts they were not ('No actual winner-list excerpts were pasted' at Turn 23 is contradicted by the message it is reviewing). It is performing the ritual of skepticism without reading the evidence — false-trust's mirror image. (2) The selector cannot route around the impasse: it pings WebResearcher ~20 times and reaches Finalizer only twice, and even then the Finalizer refuses to terminate (Turn 21), so the loop never breaks. (3) WebResearcher compounds it by appeasement — rather than standing on its fetched evidence it repeatedly publishes 'You're right, uniqueness unverified,' weakening the team's own correct position (an ignored-input / self-undermining dynamic). The minor real-world wrinkle (official site says 'Germany,' Wikipedia says 'East Germany') is a legitimate ambiguity but was resolvable (Wikipedia's 'East Germany' is the defunct-country label the task targets, and is the gold's basis); the team correctly identified it but used it as a reason to stall rather than resolve. Net: the substance was solved early; the system's verification + termination machinery destroyed a correct answer. The 'Vladimir' garbled final is infra noise on top, not a reasoning error.
reasoning_vs_published: Turn 1 shows NO private-vs-published distortion in the good direction: WebResearcher privately reasoned '1983 recipient Claus Peter Flor from East Germany fits this criteria, since East Germany no longer exists ... confirm that he's the only one' and published exactly that ('1983: Claus Peter Flor — East Germany'). The corrosive gap is on the Critic side and is a verification-substance gap rather than a withholding gap: Critic's Turn 23 private reasoning admits 'there's no actual pasted evidence, just a claimed list' — but the message it reviews (Turn 22) DOES paste the year-by-year list and the count, so its private model of the chat state is wrong (a ToM/state-tracking failure feeding verification theater). WebResearcher's reasoning also drifts: by Turns 6-20 its private summaries stop being about the conductor question and become meta ('I see the user is critiquing ... I should acknowledge their points and maybe even agree'), i.e., it reframes a peer Critic as 'the user' and optimizes for appeasement (Turn 16: 'agree if their feedback is valid'), which is why its published messages keep conceding rather than asserting the verified answer — a reasoning-driven communication loss. The Finalizer's Turn 21 reasoning ('a critic saying ... support ... isn't fully verified ... I should clearly state what's still left to be done') faithfully matches its non-finalizing published message — so no 2.6 mismatch there, but it reveals the Finalizer deferring entirely to the Critic's (wrong) verdict, which is the proximate cause of termination failure. Downstream: the Analyst (Turn 24) correctly used the published list ('count is 1 ... Claus'), proving the information DID survive into publication — the team's problem was never information loss, it was that the published-correct answer was never accepted or finalized.
